title: Quantization sensitivity sweep: calibration stability, latency vs cost tradeoffs for FP8/INT8
creator: Rohan Gupta
description:
Background: We're onboarding additional FP8 and INT8 quantization profiles for the 13B family. Initial calibration pipelines produced promising token-level accuracy but there are open questions about runtime stability when combined with our continuous batching and KV-cache behavior at long context lengths. This ticket scopes an experiment and benchmark sweep to quantify 1) calibration sensitivity across datasets and quant methods, 2) throughput/latency and GPU-efficiency tradeoffs for FP8 vs INT8 variants, and 3) interactions with batching and long-context KV caching that can cause tail-latency spikes or accuracy regression.

Goals:
- Define a deterministic calibration workflow and registry for each quant profile (FP8-A, FP8-B, INT8-symmetric, INT8-per-channel).
- Run a controlled benchmark matrix across model variants with varying batch sizes, sequence lengths (1k, 4k, 8k, 16k), and KV-cache warm/ cold scenarios.
- Measure latency percentiles (p50/p90/p99), throughput (tokens/sec), GPU util and memory, and accuracy deltas on eval prompt suites (LM loss, instruction-following accuracy, and a small QA accuracy set).
- Produce actionable rules: recommended default quant profiles per workload, guardrails (e.g., avoid INT8 for >8k unless X calibration used), and perf knobs for console suggestions.

Acceptance criteria:
- A reproducible calibration script + config for each profile checked into infra/calib/ with a short README.
- A benchmark report with: latency/throughput tables, accuracy deltas vs fp16 baseline, and per-workload guidance.
- Identified regressions and proposed mitigations (kernel fallback, dynamic dequantization, reduced batch sizes) documented in the ticket.

Measurement Plan / Test Matrix:
- Models: 13B-base (fp16 baseline), 13B-FP8-A, 13B-FP8-B, 13B-INT8-sym, 13B-INT8-pc
- Hardware: p4d.24xlarge (A100-40GB) and g5.12xlarge (A10G), plus one internal dev rig (RTX6000) for quick iterations
- Batches: [1, 4, 8, 16, 32] tokens per request measured; batching enabled in runtime with continuous batching window = 5ms and 20ms for a subset
- Sequences: [512, 1024, 4096, 8192, 16384] to capture long-context behavior
- KV-cache states: cold (first token), warm-single (cache populated on single stream), warm-multi (cache shared across multi-batched streams)
- Metrics: p50/p90/p99 latency (ms), median tokens/sec per-GPU, GPU memory (GB), peak memory, loss delta vs fp16, task-level accuracy delta (QA/Instruction), tail-latency cause analysis (profiling samples)

Calibration workflow:
- Use the calib pipeline (infra/calib/run_calib.sh) to produce per-layer scale tables. Calib dataset: 20k varied-length sequences sampled from Redwood eval corpora (mix of instruction-following, code, long-form docs).
- Store calibration artifacts in s3://redwood-calib/2026-02/ENG-21209/{profile}/{seed}.json and record checksums in the registry file.
- For INT8, test both symmetric and per-channel rounding strategies and log quantization error histograms per-layer.

Observability and analysis plan:
- Instrument runtime to emit per-request kernel timing traces, batching pack/unpack latency, and KV-cache hit/miss counters. Hook these into the temporary dashboard: https://dash.redwood.internal/boards/ENG-21209-quant-sweep (private).
- Use perf traces to correlate p99 spikes with either kernel fallbacks or large memcpy operations during KV-cache updates.

Initial results (summary):
- FP8-A: ~1.9x token/sec vs fp16 baseline at batch >=8, median-latency improved ~25% for short sequences, accuracy delta <= 0.6% LM loss on evaluation suite. Tail p99 increases at >8k sequences when batching window >10ms due to larger KV-copy overheads.
- FP8-B: slightly higher accuracy than FP8-A (+0.2% on instruction accuracy) but ~10% lower throughput in multi-batch scenarios due to additional per-token correction kernel.
- INT8-sym: best memory reduction but introduces 1.8-2.4% LM loss regression on instruction suite unless per-layer bias compensation is applied during calibration.
- INT8-pc: better accuracy than symmetric INT8 (loss delta ~1.1%) but requires per-channel scale table that increases startup time ~40ms per model load.

Key observations:
- Batching window tuning is critical: larger windows increase throughput but amplify p99 latency on long-context sequences because KV-cache copy scales with sequence length.
- Some kernels degrade for INT8 on A10G (g5) due to less optimized int8 fp kernel paths — fallback to fp16 causes unpredictable latency spikes.
- Calibration seed variability: for INT8-sym, different calibration sample seeds produced up to 0.6% LM loss variance; we need deterministic reservoir sampling and a stable seed in the registry.

Links and artifacts: [Confluence PRD] https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INFR/ENG-21209+Quant+Sensitivity+Sweep, [Calib artifacts] s3://redwood-calib/2026-02/ENG-21209/, [Benchmark dashboards] https://dash.redwood.internal/boards/ENG-21209-quant-sweep, [GH PR] https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4821, [Experiment notebook] https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1abcExampleFolder

Risks & trade-offs:
- Enabling aggressive FP8 defaults could reduce cost but may expose customers to rare correctness regressions on long-chain reasoning prompts.
- Shipping INT8-per-channel as default increases model load time and calibration complexity; we must weigh cost vs startup latency for interactive workloads.

Deliverables:
- infra/calib/* scripts + registry entries committed to runtime repo (PR above).
- Benchmark CSV artifacts under s3 bucket and an exported PDF report uploaded to Confluence.
- Short console UX proposal for runtime-1.19 recommending default profile per workload class (interactive vs high-throughput batch).
test_matrix: See 'Measurement Plan / Test Matrix' in description. Full CSV artifacts: s3://redwood-calib/2026-02/ENG-21209/batch-matrix.csv
observations: See 'Initial results (summary)' in description. FP8-A best throughput; INT8 needs compensations; batching window interacts with KV-copy leading to p99 spikes.
results_summary: FP8 tradeoffs look promising for throughput-sensitive workloads; INT8 can be used for cost-sensitive background workloads after additional calibration bias compensation. Specific guidance will be formalized in final report.
next_steps: 1) Complete remaining runs on g5 (A10G) for INT8 profile and capture fallback traces. 2) Add deterministic reservoir sampling to calib pipeline and re-run INT8 seeds. 3) Draft console recommendations and runtime guardrails. 4) Postmortem any unexpected p99 causes and propose kernel-level mitigations.
